evidence.quote: Excuse me, ah, that was my tissue on the table to reserve the seat. Can you please move so I can sit down?
Oh, I'm sorry about that! I didn't realize it was reserved. Let me move so you can sit down.
Thank you, Rachel, for understanding! It's alright, no hard feelings.
It's great to see that everyone can be understanding in these situations! How do you think we can avoid such mix-ups in the future?
Well, one solution could be to always check if a seat is reserved before sitting down. Also, maybe we can have clearer signals, like using a specific item to mark reserved seats, not just tissues.
I think those suggestions are great, Mr. Lim! Having a specific item to mark reserved seats would definitely make things clearer for everyone. I'm all for it!
I think we can consider using small, colorful flags or markers that anyone can easily spot. They shouldn't take much space and can be reusable.

I really like that idea, Mr. Lim. Colorful flags would definitely help everyone spot which seats are reserved easily. It’s a simple and effective solution! What do you all think about the design or colors we should use?
I think bright colors would work well, like red and yellow, since they grab attention quickly. Maybe we could also have some designed patterns on them so they look appealing and are easy to notice!
Nur Aisyah, I think your suggestions are spot on! Bright colors like red and yellow would definitely catch attention. Adding some fun designs could also make the markers more appealing.
